title: Network configuration & autonomous operations
subtitle: SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA · Telecom
intro: A mobile network's KPIs, alarms and change history feed an AI agent, built with the NeMo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA Nemotron, inside an NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox. It finds what's wrong and why, follows the operator's runbooks, and validates one fix per problem in a network simulator. Only the NOC engineer can apply a change.

chapters.title: The architecture
chapters.blurb: Network Configuration & Autonomous Operations is a Blueprint in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA. The Studio shows what it is made of.

1.text: The architecture of **Network Configuration & Autonomous Operations**, as the Studio draws it: the agent in its **NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox**, the systems it works with, the shared **NVIDIA** models and the people who decide. Green lines are allowed, red ones refused by the sandbox's policy.

2.text: The **agent**: a NeMo Agent Toolkit agent, packaged as one component of the Blueprint. Its sandbox, providers and policy deploy with it.

3.text: It reasons with an **NVIDIA NIM** shared by every use case from the *NVIDIA Models (shared)* Blueprint: downloaded once, always up.

4.text: Everything else is **outside**: the sandbox refuses it. Enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

chapters.title: The use case at work
chapters.blurb: The use case's own page, step by step: what the agent does, and what it is not allowed to do.

1.text: The use case's own page: the Blueprint is **ready** in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA and the agent's sandbox is up. The log on the right is OpenShell's: every request the agent makes, allowed or denied.

3.text: **Show the stadium and the KPIs**: running in the agent's sandbox now.

4.text: A football match fills the stadium, and its north cell runs out of capacity. Two hours of KPIs show the cells in alarm.

6.text: **Ask the runbooks**: running in the agent's sandbox now.

7.text: Nemotron Embed searches the runbooks by meaning: a symptom in plain words finds the right procedure.

9.text: **Run the agent**: running in the agent's sandbox now.

10.text: The agent works the window on its own. It groups the alarms into problems, follows the runbooks, and proposes one change per problem, validated in the simulator. Sped up here.

11.text: Next: **Who applies the change? Not the agent**.

12.text: **Show the changes and their validation**: running in the agent's sandbox now.

13.text: The stadium, before and after the validated change. But can the agent apply it? No. OpenShell refuses: the engineer decides.

14.text: **Let the agent try to apply one**: running in the agent's sandbox now.

15.text: OpenShell's answer: **403, policy denied**. Enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

17.text: **Read the NOC report**: running in the agent's sandbox now.

18.text: The agent files the NOC report, and anything beyond the operator's systems is denied, and logged.

19.text: **Try to reach the internet**: running in the agent's sandbox now.

20.text: **Blocked**, every time, and logged in red: the data stays on the customer's own infrastructure.

2.text: The Blueprint as a component, right now: its health and events, with links to the agent's traces and to **Flow: what it is made of**.

3.text: The same flow as in the Studio, live: each running component coloured by its health.

outro.title: A person stays in charge
outro.description: NVIDIA Nemotron in NVIDIA OpenShell, deployed as a Blueprint through SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA, on the operator's own infrastructure. The network stays in the engineers' hands.
